rv.q: Joe DiPietro's book never spirits up the true tumult of this legendary affair.
Sinatra the Musical is an inoffensive guide for newcomers.
But it's so far from exceptional. And for a big West End show with clear Broadway aspirations it should be so much better.
A lot of money has been spent here, but for what? To furnish a vehicle for the hits, which are duly trotted out, though often jarringly reframed for two mismatched voices.
That aside, what a thoroughly terrific evening of traditional musical theatre entertainment.
A good night out, more a play with Sinatra's songs as its backbone, this musical is in reliable hands.
There's a really sharp, sensitive play in there, unwritten, which haunted my imagination all through this big, blasting, powerhouse show.

cn.t: This bio-musical about Sinatra's comeback years delivers big band energy and strong performances, but critics find the book lame and misconceived, with hits awkwardly shoehorned into a formulaic rise-fall-rise narrative.
